title: By the mind alone
theme: By the mind alone is this to be obtained; there is no diversity here at all. From death to death goes the one who sees as if there were difference here.

words.context: Śaṅkara: by a mind refined by the teacher and the scripture, «आचार्यागमसंस्कृतेन»; Raṅgarāmānuja: a purified mind, «विशुद्धमनोग्राह्यम्»
Śaṅkara: «अणुमात्रमपि», not even an atom's worth; Madhva builds his reading on this word

words.role: subject of gacchati; correlative of yaḥ

sandhi.type: ā + e; a + i; m before a vowel
sandhi.rule: ā + e give ai, P. 6.1.88 (वृद्धिरेचि); a + i give e, P. 6.1.87 (आद्गुणः); a final m before a vowel is simply joined to it.
Like vowels fuse into the long vowel, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).

sandhi.type: aḥ before a vowel other than a
sandhi.rule: The visarga of -aḥ is lost before a vowel other than a, and the vowels then stay apart.

morphology.note: A gerundive of √āp, ‘obtain, reach’, with -tavya: ‘to be obtained’. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka's version of the line has anudraṣṭavyam, ‘to be seen’.
The neuter of the interrogative with cana: ‘anything at all’; with na, ‘nothing whatever’.

translation.literal: By the mind alone is this to be obtained; here there is not anything [that is] diverse. From death to death goes he who sees here as if [there were] difference.
translation.readable: It is by the mind alone that this is to be reached; here there is no diversity at all. Whoever sees anything like difference here goes from death to death.

anvaya: मनसा एव इदम् आप्तव्यम्; इह किञ्चन नाना न अस्ति । यः इह नाना इव पश्यति, सः मृत्योः मृत्युम् गच्छति ।
syntax: A gerundive clause (idam āptavyam) with the instrumental manasā restricted by eva, then a negative existential clause (na … asti kiñcana). The second line repeats 2.1.10's second line with gacchati for āpnoti.

ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: the mind refined by the teacher and scripture, before the knowledge of oneness arises, «प्रागेकत्वविज्ञानादाचार्यागमसंस्कृतेन मनसैव»; Raṅgarāmānuja: the self is to be grasped by a purified mind, «आत्मस्वरूपं विशुद्धमनोग्राह्यम्». Elsewhere the Kaṭha says the self is not reached by the mind (2.3.12), which both readings keep in view by qualifying the mind.

Śaṅkara: in Brahman there is no diversity at all, «इह ब्रह्मणि नाना नास्ति किञ्चन अणुमात्रमपि». Madhva: the word kiñcana extends the denial to any difference among the Lord's limbs, qualities and acts, and between them and him, «किञ्चनशब्दादवयवानां गुणानां क्रियाणां च परस्परं तद्वतां च भेदनिषेधार्थम्». Raṅgarāmānuja takes the line as a repetition for emphasis of 2.1.10.

metre.name: anuṣṭubh
metre.note: Counted as written, 16 and 17 syllables: the last pāda, ya iha nāneva paśyati, has nine, as in 2.1.10, because ya and iha stand apart after the lost visarga.

beginner: This verse explains how the oneness of the last verse is to be found. Not by the eyes or by arguing, but by the mind, a mind that has been prepared. Then it repeats the warning: there is no real division in what is ultimately real, and whoever sees division there goes on from death to death. Śaṅkara says the mind must first be shaped by a teacher and by the scripture; once the knowledge of oneness dawns, nothing divided remains, not even a speck. Raṅgarāmānuja says the self is grasped by a purified mind, and that the repeated line simply drives home the last verse. Madhva reads the small word ‘anything’ as ruling out any division inside God: between his limbs, his qualities and his actions, or between these and God himself.
analogy: Like finding a word one already knows by turning the mind towards it rather than searching a room: the search is inward, but it still needs a trained attention.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: This is to be reached by the mind alone; there is no diversity here at all; whoever sees difference here, as it were, goes from death to death.

commentary.q: Śaṅkara: a mind refined by teacher and scripture
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Before the knowledge of oneness arises, Brahman of one nature is to be reached by the mind alone, refined by teacher and scripture, «प्रागेकत्वविज्ञानादाचार्यागमसंस्कृतेन मनसैव इदं ब्रह्मैकरसम् आप्तव्यम्», as ‘the self alone exists, nothing else’, «आत्मैव नान्यदस्तीति». When it is reached, ignorance, which presents diversity, has ceased, so there is not even an atom of diversity in Brahman, «अणुमात्रमपि». Whoever does not give up the dim sight of ignorance goes from death to death, «स्वल्पमपि भेदमध्यारोपयन्», imposing even a little difference.

commentary.q: Raṅgarāmānuja: why the self of all is not perceived
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: He asks why the supreme Self, the self of all, is not perceived by us, «सर्वात्मभूतं परमात्मतत्वं कुतो नोपलभ्यते», and answers with the first half-verse: it is grasped by a purified mind, «आत्मस्वरूपं विशुद्धमनोग्राह्यम्». The rest repeats the point of 2.1.10 to make it firm, «उक्तमेवार्थं दृढीकरणाय अभ्यस्यति».

commentary.q: Madhva: no difference in the Lord's qualities and acts
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Madhva cites a verse he attributes to the Śabdanirṇaya on the senses of iva, «भवेदेकत्र संयोग इवशब्दोऽविरुद्धयोः», and concludes that in nāneva the word marks even a slight difference and difference-in-identity, «अतो नानेव इतीवशब्दोऽत्यल्पविषयो भेदाभेदविषयश्च». The first line of 2.1.10 denies a difference of nature in the Lord; here kiñcana extends the denial to his limbs, qualities and acts, «किञ्चनशब्दादवयवानां गुणानां क्रियाणां च परस्परं तद्वतां च भेदनिषेधार्थम्».

commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: The Bṛhadāraṇyaka has «मनसैवानुद्रष्टव्यं नेह नानास्ति किञ्चन», ‘by the mind alone is it to be seen’, where the Kaṭha has āptavyam, ‘to be reached’; its second line is the one shared with 2.1.10 (āpnoti), not this verse's gacchati.

advaita.text: Brahman, of one nature, is reached by a mind shaped by teacher and scripture; in it there is no diversity at all, «इह ब्रह्मणि नाना नास्ति किञ्चन अणुमात्रमपि».

visistadvaita.text: The supreme Self, the self of all, is grasped by a purified mind, «आत्मस्वरूपं विशुद्धमनोग्राह्यम्»; the second half repeats 2.1.10 for emphasis.

dvaita.text: ‘Nothing diverse here’ denies difference among the Lord's limbs, qualities and acts and between them and him, «तद्वतां च भेदनिषेधार्थम्» — a denial of internal difference in the Lord.

schools.disagreement: ‘No diversity here’ is absolute non-difference in Brahman for Śaṅkara, the one Self of all for Raṅgarāmānuja, and the Lord's freedom from internal difference for Madhva. The verse's own words do not decide between them.

parallels.note: The same half-verse with anudraṣṭavyam, ‘to be seen’, for āptavyam.

parallels.quote: नैव वाचा न मनसा प्राप्तुं शक्यो न चक्षुषा
parallels.note: Later the Kaṭha says the self cannot be reached by speech, mind or eye; the commentators reconcile the two by the kind of mind meant here.

contemporary.text: Some things are found only by attention of a certain quality — a melody in a noisy room, a meaning in a difficult text. The verse places its discovery in the mind, but a prepared mind, which is a claim about training rather than effort alone. This is a reflection, not a claim made by the text.

reflect.beginner: What have you understood only after your mind was ready for it?
reflect.deeper: The Kaṭha says the self is reached ‘by the mind alone’ here and ‘not by the mind’ in 2.3.12. How does each commentator hold both?
reflect.practice: Before reading one verse today, spend a minute letting the mind settle; then read it slowly once.

flags.note: Absolute non-difference (Śaṅkara), one Self of all (Raṅgarāmānuja), no internal difference in the Lord (Madhva). The Śabdanirṇaya verse is reported as cited by Madhva.
